## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*(Uttara) Pāyāsivimānavatthu* (Vv 74) is a verse narrative in the *Vimānavatthu*, translated into English under the title *Uttara Pāyāsi’s Mansion* [SuttaCentral]. In this discourse, a deity (*deva*) describes the heavenly rewards and spiritual benefits resulting from the meritorious act of offering alms food to Buddhist monks [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records five modern translations of the text in five languages [SuttaCentral].

The text shows extensive formulaic reuse characteristic of the *Vimānavatthu* corpus. According to DharmaNexus analysis, it shares 174 matching passages across 28 other Pali texts, most notably with its commentary, the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* (52 matches, spanning segments §1.1–5.3), as well as numerous other poetic narratives within the collection such as the *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), *Cittalatāvimānavatthu* (Vv 75), *Dutiyaagāriyavimānavatthu* (Vv 66), *Paṭhamakuṇḍalīvimānavatthu* (Vv 72), and *Dutiyakuṇḍalīvimānavatthu* (Vv 73) [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language matches with Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan texts are recorded by DharmaNexus at the standard reporting threshold [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
